findings.evidence: maintenance documentation will be supplied and the operating system will be tested
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits which party (Yoggie Corporation or the Web Store developers) is responsible for supplying maintenance documentation and testing the operating system.

findings.evidence: easy of use and compatibility
findings.rationale: Subjective and unquantified terms with no measurable usability threshold or defined target systems for compatibility.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: Omits the subject/actor responsible for using or enforcing the SQL-based database.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: Repeats the requirement to use a SQL-based database already stated in GJ-003.

findings.evidence: Other versions may not be 100% compatible. Also other browsers such as Mozilla or Firefox may not be 100% compatible.
findings.rationale: Non-binding 'may not be 100% compatible' and open-ended 'such as Mozilla or Firefox' leave required compatibility behavior for unlisted browsers and versions undefined.

findings.evidence: Compatibility is only tested and verified
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits which party or role performs and verifies browser compatibility testing.

findings.evidence: Shall install online help for users via the web interface
findings.rationale: Missing subject/actor; it is unspecified whether the system, installer, or administrator performs the installation.

findings.evidence: Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: Prepositional phrase attachment is ambiguous: 'for the Administrator' could apply only to 'Installation Instructions' or to all three documents, including 'Users Guide book'.

findings.evidence: Shall deliver Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions
findings.rationale: Missing subject/actor specifying who is responsible for delivering these documents.

findings.evidence: Assume the delivery of development, test and evaluate samples
findings.rationale: Phrased as an assumption ('Assume') rather than a verifiable obligation, making compliance and responsibility unclear.

findings.evidence: Assume the delivery of development, test and evaluate samples of the USB system from Yoggie.
findings.rationale: Omits the receiving actor, delivery schedule/milestone, and number of samples required for each category.

findings.evidence: Assume Yoggie will freeze the baseline of the USB system after delivery.
findings.rationale: Phrased as a non-binding assumption ('Assume') and uses 'after delivery' without specifying which delivery or timeframe.

findings.evidence: after delivery.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which delivery (sample delivery or production delivery) triggers the baseline freeze or within what timeframe it occurs.

findings.evidence: periodic backups
findings.rationale: 'Periodic' is unquantified and provides no testable backup schedule or frequency.

findings.evidence: periodic backups through a live internet connection.
findings.rationale: References recurring backups without specifying the interval/frequency, retention period, or error handling if the internet connection fails.

findings.evidence: The system shall validate credit cards against fraud.
findings.rationale: Specifies fraud validation on the happy path without defining system behavior when fraud is detected or the validation service is unavailable.

findings.evidence: all sensitive information
findings.rationale: 'Sensitive information' is undefined and open to interpretation regarding which data types and transmissions require HTTPS encryption.

findings.evidence: auto detect IP DOS attacks and block IP automatically.
findings.rationale: Omits the block timeout duration and unblocking/recovery behavior, as well as the traffic threshold that defines an IP DoS attack.

findings.evidence: The system shall detect consecutive failed login attempts.
findings.rationale: Specifies detection without stating how many consecutive failures trigger it or what resulting action, lockout duration, or recovery occurs.

findings.evidence: The system shall perform searches via Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm.
findings.rationale: Does not specify what data or entities are being searched, how the graph and edge weights are structured, or behavior when no match/path exists.

findings.evidence: 'existing' credit card
findings.rationale: Quoting 'existing' without definition leaves unclear whether this means all saved cards, the primary card on file, or the last used card.

findings.evidence: validate 'existing' credit card in system after each log in.
findings.rationale: Does not specify what happens if validation fails (e.g., expired or declined card) or when a returning customer has no stored card.

findings.evidence: too large in size
findings.rationale: Subjective, unquantified threshold with no measurable file-size or dimension criterion.

findings.evidence: compress image files that are too large in size.
findings.rationale: References a size limit without giving the numeric threshold and unit, target compressed size/quality, or failure handling for unsupported formats.

findings.evidence: on demand asynchronous loading for faster execution of pages.
findings.rationale: 'Faster execution' is an unquantified comparative without a baseline or target load time, and 'on demand' is vague about loading scope.

findings.evidence: employ on demand asynchronous loading
findings.rationale: Does not specify which pages or elements use asynchronous loading, the trigger condition, or fallback behavior if asynchronous loading fails.

findings.evidence: The system shall validate email address existence.
findings.rationale: Omits what the system does when an email address does not exist or cannot be verified, as well as when validation is triggered.

findings.evidence: easy to use
findings.rationale: Subjective, unquantified usability term with no testable acceptance criterion.

findings.evidence: easy to learn
findings.rationale: Subjective, unquantified learnability term with no measurable training time or task completion benchmark.

findings.evidence: utilize help bubbles to assist managers, customers, and administrators
findings.rationale: Does not specify which UI screens/controls have help bubbles or the user action/condition that triggers and dismisses them.

findings.evidence: easy to locate buttons
findings.rationale: 'Easy to locate' is subjective and unquantified with no measurable layout, size, or visibility metric.

findings.evidence: friend easy to read error messages
findings.rationale: 'Friend[ly] easy to read' is subjective and unquantified with no measurable readability or formatting criterion.

findings.evidence: prompt customer with friend easy to read error messages.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which error conditions trigger customer prompts or how errors for other roles are presented.

findings.evidence: consistent symbols and colors for clear notifications.
findings.rationale: 'Consistent' and 'clear' are subjective and unquantified without defining the symbol set, color palette, or contrast standards.

findings.evidence: interchangeable plugins.
findings.rationale: 'Interchangeable plugins' is vague and untestable without defining plugin interfaces, supported standards, or compatibility requirements.

findings.evidence: The system shall utilize interchangeable plugins.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which functional areas support plugins, how plugins are swapped, or error handling for incompatible plugins.

findings.evidence: easily updatable
findings.rationale: 'Easily updatable' is subjective and unquantified with no measurable time, step count, or downtime limit.

findings.evidence: The system shall be easily updatable for fixes and patches.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which actor initiates or applies updates and patches, nor the preconditions or rollback behavior on failure.

findings.evidence: easy to upgrade
findings.rationale: 'Easy to upgrade' is subjective and unquantified with no testable criteria.

findings.evidence: The system shall be easy to upgrade.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which actor performs the upgrade or under what preconditions and failure recovery rules.

findings.evidence: extremely portable
findings.rationale: 'Extremely portable' is subjective and unquantified with no measurable portability criteria or supported host environments.

findings.evidence: easy to migrate or backed up
findings.rationale: 'Easy' is subjective and unquantified with no measurable time, effort, or verification threshold.

findings.evidence: The system shall be easy to migrate or backed up via another usb drive.
findings.rationale: Does not specify which actor performs the migration or USB backup, nor preconditions or failure handling.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Non-binding modal 'should' makes whether debug mode is mandatory or optional unclear.

findings.evidence: run under debug mode.
findings.rationale: Does not specify who is authorized to enable debug mode, how it is activated, or what behavior and restrictions apply.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Non-binding modal 'should' makes mandatory requirement status unclear.

findings.evidence: run test credit card transactions.
findings.rationale: Does not specify who may run test transactions, under what mode/precondition, or how test transactions are isolated from real charges.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Non-binding modal 'should' makes mandatory requirement status unclear.

findings.evidence: run test shipping orders.
findings.rationale: Does not specify who may run test shipping orders, under what mode/precondition, or how real fulfillment is prevented.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Non-binding modal 'should' makes mandatory requirement status unclear.

findings.evidence: create test environment of weborder system.
findings.rationale: Does not specify who can create the test environment, when it is created, or what data/configuration it includes.

findings.evidence: weborder system
findings.rationale: Refers to the system as 'weborder system' instead of the established product name 'Web Store' used in earlier requirements.

findings.evidence: hardware shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection.
findings.rationale: 'Fixed and patched' is unclear as applied to physical 'system hardware' over an internet connection (e.g., whether firmware/OS patches are meant).

findings.evidence: shall be fixed and patched
findings.rationale: Passive voice omits which party or component applies and authorizes the fixes and patches, as well as failure handling if patching or connectivity fails.

findings.evidence: The system hardware shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection.
findings.rationale: Conflicts with GJ-010, which assumes Yoggie will freeze the baseline of the USB system after delivery rather than applying ongoing post-delivery hardware/system patches.

findings.evidence: coordinate on future enhancement and features with our organization.
findings.rationale: 'Coordinate' and 'future enhancement and features' are vague and untestable, and 'our organization' is an unidentified entity not defined in the document.

findings.evidence: Yoggie shall coordinate on future enhancement and features with our organization.
findings.rationale: Omits the coordination process, schedule/frequency, scope boundaries, and acceptance criteria.

findings.evidence: OS: Apache web server
findings.rationale: Lists 'Apache web server' as the OS under hardware requirements, conflicting with GJ-002 which specifies Slackware Linux 2.6 as the operating system and Apache Web Server as the web server.
